title: Layers cache ref: the composed overlay of a lock's pinned layers
location: refs/cat/layers/<key> (and the moving refs/cat/layers/main), in the INDEX repository
derivedInputs: the index's committed lock (index.lock.json), whose instances pin every layer's repository, commit, directories and digests
holds: one commit whose tree is every locked directory, declaration and asset at its mount path, exactly as mount-from-lock lays it down (no node_modules, no state mounts, nothing built at publish)
producer: the committer who changes the lock: mount:remote publishes it after a lock change, or `bun run cat layers:publish`; fallbacks: the re-pin train and the index's layers-cache workflow on main
consumers: mount-from-lock.ts (mount:lock), and through it .github/mount-from-lock.sh: the session-start hook, every CI job's mount, merge-main, the re-pin train, the prepared CI image build

refresh.how: only the instances whose lock entry moved are fetched; every layer that did not move is served from refs/cat/layers/main

savePolicy: written when the lock changes, by its writer; refused unless every mount hashes to the lock; pruned to the newest 20 lock refs plus main and every open PR's lock
verify: per instance, against the lock: the declaration's and each asset's sha256 and each directory's treeDigest (mount-from-lock layDownFrom); a layer that does not verify is fetched from its own repository, a missing ref falls back for all
uses: scripts/remote-mount.ts:2186 the committer's publish after a lock change
notes: Supersedes lpc-cat-mount and the other cat-mount Actions caches. Untrusted but exactly verified, so a stale or tampered ref only costs time. Measured on folio-assistant's lock (12 layers, ~32k files): 69 s per repository against 27 s on a hit with every byte verified. Every target needs it (it is the root of every needs closure), so it carries no `materializes`.

stateInputs.how: by construction: the ref holds every locked directory with no state mounts (mount-from-lock layDownFrom), and its key is the lock alone
